messages:
jonas: Noticed weird divergence between p50/p95/p99 on the latency dashboard for the merged endpoint view (p50 steady, p99 spikes). Anyone else?
kevin: same. p50 unchanged but p99 jumps ~3x when viewing 'All regions' merge. Breaking down by region the spike disappears.
zara: could be duplicate samples from retries or fanout (same request replicated across backends) causing heavy upper-tail skew in merged quantiles.
maria gomez: pulled raw samples for the window:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 'https://telemetry.internal/v1/metrics/samples?endpoint=/v1/generate&from=1746006600&to=1746007200' | jq . | head -n 10
# example: {"ts":1746006723, "latency_ms": 1200, "request_id":"req_42", "replica":1}
```
kevin: yep there are multiple rows with same request_id but different replica/retry flags. When we t-digest-merge across regions we inadvertently count them all.
jonas: two-layer problem: (1) dedup by logical request_id before aggregation would solve it, (2) t-digest merging assumes independent samples; duplicates bias higher quantiles.
azara: UX/console angle: users expect endpoint-level percentiles to represent single user-per-request latencies, not inflated fanout artifacts. We should default to a dedupe mode in the merged endpoint view.
alex: ingestion vs query-time: ingest dedupe (idempotent) permanently alters historical aggregates which is dangerous. Query-time transform keeps raw immutable and is reversible. But query-time can be expensive for large rollups.
maria gomez: quick micro-bench: running dedupe-by-request_id as a streaming grouping adds ~15% CPU on our metrics worker and +85ms per 200k-sample query. Added numbers to the PR draft.
kevin: API design suggestion: add a query param dedupe_by=(none|request_id|session_id) plus aggregation_mode=(tdigest|raw|deduped) so clients can opt-in. Console can set defaults.
jonas: also need to document the effect on p50 vs p99; dedupe mainly impacts high quantiles but can shift medians if retries are systematically slow.
zara: small UX: show an "aggregation provenance" chip next to each series that says e.g. "merged (dedup=request_id)" and on hover expands to the transform chain (tdigest merge -> dedupe -> interpolation).
maria gomez: opened PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/telemetry/pulls/1850 1 adds dedupe_by query param + server-side opt-in. Implementation uses a last-value-per-request grouping during query expansion.
alex: two concerns: (1) t-digest merge path tests - dedupe must run before digesting to avoid bias, (2) we need a changelog and a migration doc for customers relying on raw merged percentiles.
kevin: test plan: add synthetic harness with duplicated high-latency samples and assert p99 collapses when dedupe_by=request_id. Also add an integration that compares historical numbers before/after to produce a 'delta' report customers can opt into.
jonas: comment on PR: ensure we preserve deterministic tie-breaker for which sample wins when deduping (e.g., min latency or first seen). That policy affects SLO calculations.
zara: UX: per-tenant default toggle in Console (Settings -> Telemetry) so large customers can keep raw or prefer deduped by default. Also add a one-click banner when dashboard shows >5% delta vs last-hour to call out aggregation mode.
maria gomez: updated PR with deterministic policy: choose smallest latency per request_id by default (safe for SLOs). Benchmarks appended: dedupe stream + tdigest ~ +12% CPU and +90ms on 200k samples.
sre-bot: :white_check_mark: staging deploy succeeded for telemetry at 1746009000
alex: plan: (1) land telemetry query param but default off, (2) Console turns it on for merged endpoint views with visible provenance, (3) run canary comparing raw vs deduped across tenants for one week, (4) prepare docs + changelog.
kevin: I'll draft the changelog note and the delta-report endpoint.
jonas: I'll add unit/regression tests for the merge path and a perf test harness.
zara: I'll prototype the provenance chip and settings toggle.
maria gomez: I'll finish the PR cleanup and schedule the staging canary for tomorrow.
alex: thanks team. Quick follow-up: consider adding an api field that returns sample_origin info so dashboards can render split series (raw vs deduped) side-by-side for debugging.
kevin: good idea. Side-by-side will help product teams trust the transformation.
maria gomez: filed follow-up issue: https://git.internal/r/redwood/telemetry/issues/778
sre-bot: :rotating_light: alert: watchdog detected p99 delta > 10% for tenant 'bigbank' after running dedupe canary at 1746012000
alex: we'll triage canary alerts and iterate. Thanks all.
